title: PSUB Operator Guide
subtitle: Building Python security releases on Windows with the PSUB web UI
notes: Hero slide uses the repository background asset.

title: What PSUB Does
subtitle: A practical operator workflow from preflight to deliverables
body: Validate prerequisites
Point PSUB at extracted CPython source
Prepare the documentation virtual environment
Launch the build in a dedicated terminal
Review logs and collect EXE, MSI, and embed artifacts
callouts: Primary operator path is the local web UI on port 8080.
CLI remains available for repeatable scripted runs.
notes: Derived from README.md and the UI script.

title: Before You Start
subtitle: Environment prerequisites to clear before opening PSUB
body: Visual Studio 2019 or 2022 with Desktop development with C++
MSVC toolchains including x64, x86, and ARM64
Windows 10 SDK 10.0.19041.0 or later
Bootstrap Python 3.10 or 3.12
Git for Windows on PATH
.NET Framework 3.5 for legacy Python 3.10 MSI flows
callouts: PSUB highlights missing items and links directly to setup guides.
Do not use Python 3.13 as the bootstrap interpreter.

title: Launch PSUB
subtitle: Start the local web UI and open it in a browser
body: Run .\Script\Build-PythonRelease-UI-Simple.ps1 -Port 8080
Open http://localhost:8080/
The build itself opens in a new terminal window with live output
callouts: Default operator entry point is the web UI rather than the CLI script.

title: Check Prerequisites
subtitle: Use the left-side panel as your environment readiness gate
body: Refresh the prerequisite check when the machine changes
Read the summary banner before entering any build values
Follow setup-guide links for missing tools or SDK components
callouts: The panel covers Visual Studio, toolchains, SDK, bootstrap Python, and Git.

title: Prepare Build Settings
subtitle: Standard settings define the reusable defaults for each run
body: Keep the documentation venv name at doc-venv unless you have a reason to change it
Choose the release output directory where final packages and zip files should land
Set the Windows SDK version expected by the CPython build
Use Setup Virtual Environment before the first build on a new source tree
callouts: PSUB can create or update the documentation venv from the UI.

title: Configure and Start a Build
subtitle: Fill in the CPython source and bootstrap interpreter, then launch
body: SourcePath must point at the extracted CPython root containing PCbuild and Tools\msi
Bootstrap Python must be 3.10 or 3.12
Use Auto-Detect to prefill a compatible local Python path
Start Build opens a dedicated terminal and PSUB polls build status in the page
callouts: The UI blocks empty SourcePath and BootstrapPython values before it starts the build.

title: Monitor Logs and Results
subtitle: Use inline status and the log viewer to validate the run
body: Open Latest Log to inspect the captured run output
Watch button and status-color changes for running, success, or failure states
Collect release artifacts from the configured release root and CPbuild\amd64\en-us
callouts: If a real build state is not staged, use the screenshot with the log button highlighted and explain the expected transitions.

title: Common Failure Cases
subtitle: Most blocked runs fall into a small set of operator-fixable issues
body: Git missing from PATH
Windows SDK or MSVC toolchains not fully installed
Wrong bootstrap Python version
Missing doc-venv or missing Sphinx dependencies
Python 3.10 WiX /.NET 3.5 dependency problem
buildrelease.bat reports Build FAILED even when exit code is 0
callouts: Install Git for Windows and restart the shell.
Use the setup guides linked by the prerequisites panel.
Run Setup Virtual Environment or install Doc\requirements.txt into the venv.
Enable .NET Framework 3.5 and rerun MSI externals for 3.10 flows.
Trust PSUB's output-based failure guard instead of the batch file exit code alone.

title: Standard Operator Workflow
subtitle: The repeatable PSUB sequence for a clean release run
body: Verify prerequisites
Open the UI
Confirm environment health
Set SourcePath and BootstrapPython
Create or refresh doc-venv
Start the build
Review the log
Collect the final artifacts
callouts: This sequence aligns with the repo runbook and keeps failures visible early.
